# WCA square-1 and clock geometry fixtures

Source artifacts, retrieved 2026-10-10 and stored verbatim:

- WCA regulations (single-file markdown, canonical source of the WCA): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thewca/wca-regulations/main/wca-regulations.md, mirror of https://regulations.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/, saved at playground/sq1_probe/wca/wca-regulations.md, sha256 c850df1d2b8c912e34ec84f107079fcfadbc1318ceef2607bfc12c5b64f30e26.
- Official clock scrambler: https://github.com/thewca/tnoodle-lib/blob/main/scrambles/src/main/java/org/worldcubeassociation/tnoodle/puzzle/ClockPuzzle.java, saved at playground/clock_probe/tnoodle/ClockPuzzle.java, sha256 b1d373eb2ed1e7209ca2cf1ab0b3430c7af96cf38190e07a578622a3398314f5.
- Official square-1 scrambler: https://github.com/thewca/tnoodle-lib/blob/main/scrambles/src/main/java/org/worldcubeassociation/tnoodle/puzzle/SquareOnePuzzle.java, saved at playground/sq1_probe/tnoodle/SquareOnePuzzle.java, sha256 fe3e876c38ac7a50f93e145a433dfa9273c1ace35c49deff04c181d3df0088ee.

Regulation text, quoted verbatim from wca-regulations.md:

- 12c) Notation for Square-1:
  - 12c1) Moves are applied with one of the two smallest surfaces of the equatorial slice on the left side of the front face.
  - 12c2) (X, Y) means: turn upper layer X times 30 degrees clockwise, turn bottom layer Y times 30 degrees clockwise. X and Y must be integers from -5 to 6, and cannot be both equal to 0.
  - 12c3) "/" means: turn the right half of the puzzle 180 degrees.
  - 12c4) Metric for Square-1: (X, Y) counts as one move, "/" counts as one move.
- 12g) Notation for Clock:
  - 12g1) The puzzle is oriented with 12 o'clock on top, and either side in front.
  - 12g2) Move pins up: UR (top-right), DR (bottom-right), DL (bottom-left), UL (top-left), U (both top), R (both right), D (both bottom), L (both left), ALL (all).
  - 12g3) Turn a wheel next to an up-position pin and move all pins down afterwards: X+ (X clockwise turns), X- (X counter-clockwise turns).
  - 12g4) Turn around the puzzle so that 12 o'clock stays on top, and then move all pins down: y2.

Model conventions, verified against the scrambler sources above:

Square-1 state is 2 unit rings of 12 slots. The solved rings are top {0,0,1,2,2,3,4,4,5,6,6,7} and bottom {8,9,9,10,11,11,12,13,13,14,15,15}, each entry the piece id occupying that 30 degree unit, corners spanning 2 units, edges 1. A twist (X,Y) moves top content at unit u to (u+X) mod 12 and bottom content at unit v to (v+Y) mod 12, matching doRotateTopAndBottom in SquareOnePuzzle.java with the WCA clockwise senses: top clockwise viewed from above, bottom clockwise viewed from below. A slash is legal exactly when both rings have piece boundaries at the 11|0 and 5|6 junctions, matching canSlash, and swaps top units 6..11 with bottom units 6..11 index for index, matching doSlash, toggling the equatorial half orientation. Twist ids enumerate the 143 pairs (X,Y) in [-5,6]x[-5,6] minus (0,0) in row-major order with the (0,0) hole removed, slash is id 143.

Square-1 stickers are 48 fixed slots: side slot (layer, unit) at indices 0..23, one per unit, and face anchor slot (layer, unit) at indices 24..47, the up or down face patch anchored at the first unit of the occupying piece. Side and anchor slots ride their unit: a twist maps slot (l,u) to (l,u+turn), a slash maps (top,u) to (bottom,u) and back for u in 6..11, both per block. Because the unit carry rule is uniform, both mappings are shape independent, the shape state only gates slash legality, so the pure move_facelets entry serves twists and returns CT_GEOMETRY_E_STATE for the slash, and the state-aware entry checks canSlash. The 8 face anchors per layer that no piece starts at in a given shape are permanently empty slots. World embedding: azimuth 0 at front, increasing clockwise viewed from above, top unit u centered at azimuth 30u+15, bottom unit v at 165-30v, which makes the slash a 180 degree rotation of the swapped half about the front axis and the bottom twist sense clockwise viewed from below. Slot positions use the 12 point ring table in geometry_sq1.c at radius 2 lattice scale, side slots at y +-1 with radial normals, face anchors at y +-2 with vertical normals. Piece orientation (corner twist carried by slash flips) is outside the permutation abstraction and not modeled.

Clock state is 18 hand positions mod 12, front row-major UL,U,UR,L,C,R,DL,D,DR at indices 0..8, back same layout in the back's own view at 9..17. The official move vectors in ClockPuzzle.java encode this rule, restated: a wheel turn with pin set P adds the amount to every front clock adjacent to an up pin, that is for each up corner the corner clock, its two neighboring edge clocks, and the center, and subtracts it from each back corner clock at the same world corner, corner pairs being geared opposite. Back grid index of front corner (r,c) is 9+3r+(2-c). Wheel turn names are UR,DR,DL,UL,U,R,D,L,ALL per 12g2, U meaning both top pins, and so on. Canonical amounts are 0+..6+ and 1-..5- per the successor table and generateRandomMoves, 12 forms per name, move ids name*12+form, y2 is id 108. y2 swaps the front and back arrays index for index and flips the puzzle, matching getSuccessorsByName. Clock world positions reuse the 3x3 cube F and B face frames: front clock i at F (i/3,i%3), back clock at B ((i-9)/3,(i-9)%3), consistent with y2 being a 180 rotation about the vertical axis. Wheel turns have no permutation of positions, they change hand angles, so move_facelets returns CT_GEOMETRY_E_PERM for them and the permutation for y2 only. All 18 affected hands of a wheel turn rotate about the front axis, y2 about the vertical axis.

Grammar scope: square-1 tokens are exactly "(X,Y)" with strict integers and "/", clock tokens are exactly name, one digit, sign per the canonical forms plus "y2". Site notations beyond the WCA scramble grammar are out of scope and rejected: Sarah's cubing.net setup markers (U), (U'), (D) and trailing *, and cubingapp's paren-less "3,3" form, all present in db/seeds/packs/sq1_*.tsv recorded 2026-10-10. Pin-only tokens of 12g2 are not scramble moves, 12i1 excludes pin changes from moves, and are not parsed.
